subject: MSA / Order Form: term mechanics, auto-renew exceptions and notice sequencing
messages:
From: Jamie Ortiz <jamie.ortiz@velasystems.com>
To: Logan Wright <logan.wright@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 17 Nov 2026 09:12:00 -0800
Subject: MSA + Order Form: term / auto-renew / notice

Hi Logan,

Thanks again for the walkthrough this morning. Procurement ran a quick legal review of the MSA and Order Form and they returned a few high-level asks we need to resolve before we can take this to commercial approval:

1) Auto-renew: Vela is not comfortable with unconditional auto-renew beyond the first term. Would you consider a mutual auto-renew only if either party provides notice within a defined window (we suggested 60 days), or alternatively we opt for explicit renewal rather than automatic rollovers?

2) Notice windows: For termination for convenience (TFC) we propose a 60-day notice if invoked during active term, but 90 days if invoked within 60 days of an auto-renew trigger. They want predictable time to switch providers and align procurement cycles.

3) Termination for Convenience scope: Procurement is asking that TFC explicitly exclude active pilots under $50k or that pilots have a shorter notice/credit mechanic.

I've attached their redlines (Vela_redlines_20261117.pdf) that highlight the three areas above. Can you concede to mutual notice (our acceptance of a mutual 60/90 ladder) or share Redwood's preferred compromise language? Also please advise on standard internal approval cadence for any deviations to our auto-renew default.

Jamie
Jamie's signature
Director, Strategic Sourcing
Vela Systems

Quick commercial math and recommended options:

Baseline impact (approx):
- If we accept 60-day mutual notice: expected short-term churn risk +1.8% ARR on this cohort; average support ramp-up cost ~$12k per terminated customer.
- If we accept 90-day mutual notice: churn risk drops to +0.9%; cost impact is smaller but slows ability for customers to exit quickly.

Options to offer to customer (ranked):
1) Mutual 90-day notice, with a limited one-time 60-day opt-in for the first renewal only (covers conversions from pilot).
2) Keep Redwood standard (auto-renew each year unless partner gives 30 days' notice) but offer a pilot carveout: pilots < $50k get a 30-day notice and pro-rated credit on unused months.
3) Mutual 60-day, but require a higher minimum committed spend or introduce a termination fee to offset churn risk.

Operational asks: I can model the exact impact if legal finalizes the clause. Attached my quick workbook.

-ben
Ben Carter
Head of Commercial Operations, Redwood Inference

Date: Wed, 18 Nov 2026 09:38:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Fwd: MSA + Order Form: term / auto-renew / notice

Thanks — read the redlines. Legal's suggested compromise language below (clean, for customer-facing redline):

"Termination for Convenience. Either party may terminate the applicable Order Form or the MSA for convenience upon providing written notice no less than ninety (90) days prior to the effective date of termination; provided, however, that if such notice is given within sixty (60) days prior to an automatic renewal date, the notice period shall be sixty (60) days. Notwithstanding the foregoing, pilot engagements with total fees under Fifty Thousand Dollars (USD $50,000) shall be subject to a thirty (30) day convenience notice and Redwood shall provide a pro rata service credit for unused, prepaid services."

Notes:
- This mirrors Vela's ladder but preserves our tiering for pilots and gives us a carveout we can measure.
- We should avoid unconditional mutual 30-day auto-renew opt-outs — that increases risk. Instead propose opt-in toggles for pilot conversions.
- If Commercial wants a shorter notice for enterprise deals, we need an Executive Exception. Kimberly, please advise the approver and timeline.

I'll attach a plaintext snippet for the redline file. If we get buy-in I'll prepare a tracked-changes version to send back to the customer.

Marcus Lin
Senior Counsel, Redwood Inference

Jamie — thanks for the clear redlines and context. Appreciate the candid ask from Procurement. After internal review, here's Redwood's proposed compromise. If acceptable we'll produce a tracked redline and a DocuSign packet for signature: 

Proposed redline (summary):
- Mutual notice ladder: 90-day notice as standard; if notice is given within 60 days of an automatic renewal date the notice period will be 60 days.
- Pilots under $50k: 30-day notice plus pro rata credit for any unused prepaid months.
- Auto-renew mechanics: Auto-renew remains in place but Redwood will add a clear notification 120 days prior to renewal and a one-time opt-out toggle for customers converting from pilot to committed terms (must be exercised no later than 30 days prior to renewal).

Ben has modeled the cost tradeoffs and Marcus has prepared the attached legal language. If Vela is comfortable with this framing we will send a tracked redline and a DocuSign link.

Next steps:
1) Please confirm whether the laddered 90/60 notice with the pilot 30-day carveout is acceptable.
2) If yes, confirm point of contact for signature and preferred cadence for execution (e.g., are you OK with DocuSign?).

I'm attaching the proposed redline PDF for quick review.

Thanks — Logan
